0.0.n: Sets the time for the evening routine.

0.1.n: Marks nighttime as the topic of this part of the story.

0.2.n: A familiar, affectionate way to refer to a father.

0.3.n: Marks Papa as the person sharing the meal.

0.4.n: Can mean rice or a meal; the nighttime setting makes it dinner here.

0.5.n: Marks ご飯 as what the speaker eats.

0.6.n: The て-form of 食べる links eating to the next action.

0.8.n: This is a name; Mia is another recipient of food.

0.9.n: Marks Mia as the recipient of the food.

0.10.n: Adds Mia to those being fed, following the speaker’s meal with Papa.

0.11.n: Used for food given to animals rather than people.

0.12.n: Marks 餌 as what the speaker gives.

0.13.n: The て-form of あげる connects giving food with the continuing routine.

1.0.n: The plain form of 寝る describes what happens around the time indicated by 頃.

1.1.n: Follows 寝る to indicate approximately when the speaker goes to bed.

1.2.n: Marks bedtime as the point reached with なる.

1.3.n: Together with 頃に, describes the arrival of bedtime.

1.4.n: Introduces a result that regularly happens when bedtime arrives.

1.6.n: This is the first part of the name えのき, incorrectly split into separate subtitle tokens.

1.7.n: This is the middle of the name えのき, not the particle の.

1.8.n: き completes the name えのき; が marks Enoki as the one waking up.

1.9.n: The て-form of 起きる connects to くる, presenting Enoki’s waking as something that happens around the speaker.

1.10.n: This is くる + explanatory んだ, not くるむ; it presents Enoki’s waking as part of the routine.

2.1.n: The て-form of 出す makes a casual request; the long ending suggests a drawn-out plea.

2.4.n: A casual quotation marker introducing the message Enoki seems to communicate.

2.5.n: アピールする means to signal or appeal; てくる makes the action directed toward the speaker.

2.6.n: Gives Enoki’s plea as the reason for the speaker’s next action.

3.0.n: A loanword meaning ball; here it refers to the pet’s exercise ball.

3.1.n: Marks the ball as the destination when placing Enoki inside.

3.2.n: 入れる + てあげる presents putting Enoki inside as a favor; the final て connects to the next action.

3.4.n: Refers to the time Enoki spends in the exercise ball.

3.5.n: Marks that interval as the time when the cleaning and preparation happen.

3.6.n: Refers to the pet’s toilet area, which the speaker cleans.

3.7.n: Combines with トイレ to name the task of cleaning the toilet.

3.8.n: Joins toilet cleaning and food preparation as two tasks.

3.9.n: Names the animal food the speaker prepares.

3.10.n: Links 餌 to 準備, showing what is being prepared.

3.11.n: A noun that combines with をする to describe preparing something.

3.12.n: Marks the combined cleaning and preparation tasks as what the speaker does.

3.13.n: Turns the preceding task nouns into actions with を.

3.14.n: Sentence-ending の adds a casual explanatory tone to the description of the routine.

4.0.n: The たら-form of 終わる sets finishing the tasks as the condition for the next action.

4.2.n: This is the first part of the name えのき, not a separate word.

4.3.n: This completes the name えのき, which has been split across subtitle tokens.

4.4.n: Marks Enoki as the one the speaker puts back.

4.6.n: Marks the cage as the destination when returning Enoki.

4.7.n: The て-form of 戻す links returning Enoki to the end of the routine.

4.9.n: A casual expression signaling that the routine is finished.

0.lit: At night, with Papa, eat dinner, and to Mia also give food, and…
0.tip: The て-form connects actions in a sequence without ending the sentence.

1.lit: When it becomes around sleeping time, Enoki comes awake, you see.
1.tip: Read えのき as one name and くるんだ as くる + んだ, despite the misleading token splits.

2.lit: Because she makes an appeal toward me saying, Let me out!
2.tip: って casually quotes the message the speaker imagines Enoki is communicating.

3.lit: Put her into the ball for her, and during that time do toilet cleaning and food preparation, you see.
3.tip: Verb + てあげる presents an action as something done for someone’s benefit.

4.lit: When finished, return Enoki to the cage, and all done.
4.tip: The たら-form here means when an action is completed, rather than an uncertain if.
